definitions.explanation: Refers to beef or other meat with fine streaks of fat running through it, resembling frost. Highly prized in Japanese cuisine for its tenderness and flavor.
A pattern or appearance resembling frost, used to describe textiles, ceramics, or other surfaces with a speckled white-on-dark pattern.

examples.japanese: {霜降|しもふ}りの{肉|にく}を{買|か}った。
この{霜降|しもふ}り{和牛|わぎゅう}はとても{柔|やわ}らかい。
examples.english: This marbled wagyu beef is very tender.

examples.japanese: {霜降|しもふ}りの{入|はい}った{高級|こうきゅう}な{牛肉|ぎゅうにく}をすき{焼|や}きにした。
examples.english: We made sukiyaki with high-grade marbled beef.

examples.japanese: {霜降|しもふ}りの{着物|きもの}を{着|き}た。
examples.english: She wore a kimono with a frost pattern.

examples.japanese: この{皿|さら}は{霜降|しもふ}り{模様|もよう}が{美|うつく}しい。
examples.english: This plate has a beautiful frosted pattern.

examples.japanese: {白|しろ}と{灰色|はいいろ}の{霜降|しもふ}りの{生地|きじ}でコートを{仕立|した}てた。
examples.english: The coat was tailored from a white and gray heathered fabric.

notes: When referring to meat, {霜降|しもふ}り describes the fine white fat marbling that runs through red meat, creating a pattern that looks like frost ({霜|しも}). This marbling is a key quality indicator for Japanese beef, especially {和牛|わぎゅう}. The word comes from {霜|しも} (frost) + {降|ふ}り (falling). In the textile sense, it refers to a heathered or speckled pattern. Common collocations include {霜降|しもふ}り{肉|にく} (marbled meat) and {霜降|しもふ}り{和牛|わぎゅう} (marbled wagyu).
